chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa ibn Uqayl, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding testifying to the testimony of a man who is present in the city, he said: 'Yes, and even if he is behind a pillar, that is permissible if he is unable to present himself and establish his testimony due to an impediment preventing him from attending and establishing it; so there is no harm in establishing the testimony upon the testimony.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to testify to another witness's testimony if that witness is present but unable to appear in court?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) validates the mechanism of 'testimony upon testimony' (shahadah 'ala shahadah) when a primary witness is present in the city but physically unable to appear in court due to a valid impediment. This ruling, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the jurisprudential principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) while maintaining the integrity of evidence, ensuring that justice is not obstructed by mere physical absence.
